verdict.tagline: Fluid monster hunting trapped behind severe technical and performance hurdles.
for_you_if: you want smooth and satisfying weapon combat
you are willing to push past rough optimization
not_for_you_if: you need stable frame rates on release hardware
you want a challenging early campaign
you refuse to deal with sudden technical crashes

distortion_flags.sentence: Positive review proportions increase substantially as playtime grows.
Recent reviews skew more positive than the lifetime average.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience performance issues such as low frame rates, severe stuttering during zone changes, and high resource usage even on low settings.

citations.review_text: Terribly unoptimised game that on lowest wouldn’t even sustain 60fps.

Yeah the optimization is terrible, and even on medium the stuttering is real. Cant even finish the first few hunts without so much stuttering. FPS are stable then what i believe is the engine, starts to fart all around on zone changes, it feels clunky, including UI.

World is where is at, and i personally recommend that one over Wilds. Is always on Discount, still with a lot of players and is just more fun and better first impression.

Wilds feels like a Hollywood adaptation of Monster Hunter, and in a bad way. Yeah yeah sure, nice cinematics and the npc follows you around, you speak and the game treats you like a kid that needs guide or it will get lost in the mall. No, not my style.

Monster Hunter has had some really great releases lately. In my opinion, Monster Hunter World: Iceborne was Capcom's best release back on the PS4, which gave me high expectations for this game, or at least similar ones. Unfortunately, Wilds turned out to be a lot worse than I expected.

Right from the start, the audio in the opening cutscene kept cutting out, and there was noticeable stuttering even on the default graphics settings. On default settings, the game uses far too much of my GPU. It is poorly optimized and extremely resource-intensive. The graphics themselves are not impressive either. My main issue is the lack of environmental detail and the lighting colors. The game feels very dull, with poor brightness and a washed-out color palette. It uses far too many resources yet delivers a lot less than World, which was much better optimized, had better lighting, and offered impressive changing environments and map variety. The maps here are bland and monotonous, so having your mount auto-pilot you everywhere just highlights how little there is worth stopping to see.

Character customization is a bit worse than in World. There is no clear separation between male and female characters; you are given a single base model and can apply any voice or features, which is quite messed up. It means your female model can have the voice and face of a male model and vice versa, unless you put in a lot of work to change every little facial and voice detail. In World, the female character had a certain set of features and the male had his own, making customization a lot easier. Hairstyles and faces feel mediocre compared to World, which offered plenty of good options. This game offers too little overall for character creation, and the same can be said about the voices.

That lack of identity carries into the story and protagonist. I was not really impressed with Monster Hunter World's story, but this one is a lot less impressive. The plot just is not interesting at all. The pro…

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the Seikret mount automatically navigates to monsters, removing the traditional tracking and exploration mechanics found in past titles.

citations.review_text:
The long-awaited sequel to world, and a long awaited purchase for me (bought ~50%) off.
Pros:
- More monsters, and more types of monsters than world, features octopi, spiders and leviathans unlike world which is really neat variety, nu udra and AT uth duna are highlights for me
- More of an emphasis on "smaller scale," monsters with less elder dragons, really makes the 1 (current) elder dragon encounter so memorable when its the only one. ELDERS FINALLY HAVE AURA (Unlike kirin in world...)
- Wound system is genuinely fun, with an investment to trigger big damage, reminds me a lot of the wirebugs in rise where it currently makes our hunters super strong, and like rise I hope it gets more risks involved in ascendance (like how monsters scaled in strength in sunbreak to make insane encounters)
- Equipping two weapons is a neat system, encouraging capcom to create monsters with 2 elemental weaknesses at different times, encouraging more preparations which is a highlight of MH to me

Cons:
The seikret:
- Auto follows scoutflies, making the actual "tracking," minigame I appreciated in world completely pointless. In world, mounts were unlocked behind area specific quests, so you'd gain access to them when you'd "mastered" a location already, this system really harms the exploration aspect of the game as you can just "auto navigate" to a location immediately.
- Forces maps to be so much more open and less dense, which works in certain places (the dunes in the desert, and the floating rock area in the snow) but really suffers in the rest of the map design and makes getting to a monster annoying for little reason.

Final notes on my performance experience (for anyone on the fence)
4060ti x 9600x (Original Setup)
Ran on 1440p Balanced DLSS 4 upscaling (All settings low / med)
~40-60fps

9070XT x 9600x (Current)
1440p Native, maxed settings raytracing
~60-80fps


TLDR: Buy, especially ON SALE. This game is on sale like 2/3's of the year for ~40-50% off. So if you can get it for…

I've read through other reviews and even decided against buying this game for a while because I was scared to play a "bad" Monster Hunter game. If you are looking for the next Monster Hunter: World, you may find yourself disappointed. But if you want a fun experience absolutely dominating monster after monster, then you've met your mark. This game feels less like a game for long-time fans and more like a game for up-and-comers in the franchise. An exception, not the rule.

To the player who loves a challenge, Wilds does take a while to throw something at you that feels inherently challenging. I see a lot of remarks in regard to the story, but to me, the storyline is actually decent and kept me engaged. The cinematics are breathtaking at times and the overall design of each monster is incredible. The atmosphere is beautiful and ever since the performance updates, the game has definitely improved visually.

The weapons are fleshed out rather well. The combat is more forgiving, but I found myself very eager to try new weapons again and finally putting away the ol' Insect Glaive after 3 games of devotion. I enjoy the bow very much and find it to be one of the more compelling (albeit easier) weapons to play.

No more wire-bugs (RIP), but you return to your slinger from MHWorld instead. The Seikret is a nice addition, though I do miss the tracking. Finding a monster in a massive map in World was rewarding after tracking it down to its last footstep, and that experience is missing here. Being able to walk right up to a monster within a couple of minutes or less is actually pretty sad.

The drive to explore the map looking for things has also been cut back in lieu of more monster action. Each quest is a new hunt, and you are oftentimes thrown into that hunt via the storyline, so you rarely even have to find your quarry, let alone explore the map before you do.

There are some major negatives here, but overall the game is fun. It's a great entry to play solo, and even more f…

Wilds feels like one step forward, two steps back.

There are things I liked, but more things I didn't. The character creator is better, the armor sets are extremely cool, so are the monsters, and I enjoyed the story [i]at first[/i].

Pretty quickly, though, I got tired of the unskippable Seikret rides and Marvel-esque dialogue. The game constantly shouts [b]"LOOK AT IT!"[/b]

Follow this NPC. Slowly ride behind that NPC. Watch another travel scene. Listen to more dialogue. Sit through another cutscene. So much of the game also feels like a tutorial. It took around 15 hours before the game finally stopped holding my hand.

My main problem is that Wilds automates the parts of Monster Hunter I liked, while keeping the annoying parts manual. The Seikret auto travel is convenient and useful sometimes, but it completely kills exploration. You barely need to learn the map or find the monster. You select it, and your mount drives you there like a taxi.

Finding monsters in World could be time-consuming, but I didn't mind it. It encouraged patience and, more importantly, exploration. You gradually learned the maps, noticed landmarks and started understanding where monsters were likely to go. Wilds mostly removes that process.

But somehow, after automating all of that, I still need to click through five different menus just to refill my items and restore my loadout. Maybe automate [i]that[/i] part instead?

The maps also feel bland. Everything looks grey and washed out. Technically, the areas are different, with deserts, forests and other biomes, but they don't really [i]feel[/i] distinct. The areas are bigger, but I remember the locations in World much more clearly. In Wilds, most of the environments blend together, especially when the game automatically drives you through them.

That said, most of the world is actually good when you choose to slow down and explore it yourself. There are plenty of interesting areas, creatures and small details to find. The problem is that …

citations.review_text: Feels terrible on PC and takes a lot of getting used to. Feels clunky af like it's dragged over from some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ mobile platform or console without much care for PC players. Even sheathing weapon or ESPECIALLY taking out healing potion feels TERRIBLE on PC. Whole UI feels like it was made for console and that they just slapped it on PC without doing any decent rework that would actually feel somewhat decent on PC. Soooo ♥♥♥♥. Then again some minus points for devs having brain damage while making awful quests like Lured by Abundance.

If I could give this game a mixed review I would. The game was fun up until the "Capture the Yian Kut-ku" quest. The game hardly gives you any explanation on how to properly do the capture mechanic, and on top of that, you need to face three enemies at once when trying to learn it. Maybe it's just a steep learning curve, but it's a learning curve done wrong.

That pretty much sums up this entire game. Some mechanics are explained in depth, others aren't explained at all. The weapons are fun to use, and there are some really unique monsters to fight, but the control inputs can be very wonky at times. For example, I'm often hitting the button three or four times to try and get a heal off because it just won't register. And don't even get me started on the UI... it's harder to navigate than the actual monster fights.

The game can be fun, more so with friends, but it is also one of the most frustrating games I have ever played in my life.

claims.claim: The game suffers from poor optimization, requiring hardware upgrades, performance patches, or mods to achieve acceptable frame rates and stability.

citations.review_text: It's a AAA Monhun game that looks godawful. Performance went from an utter disaster at launch to something approaching acceptable now, but it really isn't enough for how much time has passed. The gameplay isn't as bad as some might want you to think, but there's a lot of immersion and small gameplay things that got bulldozed for a more AAA experience, which really detracts from the special feel of Monhun games in the past. This is definitely a side-grade at best, and not really worth playing unless you're a diehard Monhun fan that has to play each one. I really hope the expansion makes things better, but at this point, I'm extremely doubtful.

One Year Later: Still Broken
I deliberately waited over a year before purchasing this game, genuinely believing the developers would have ironed out the notorious optimization issues by now. I was completely wrong. Intermittent performance drops, stuttering, and severe instability plague my sessions regardless.

Cross-Platform Instability
To ensure this wasn't an OS conflict, I thoroughly tested the game across both Windows and Linux. The results are identical. Even using a 9070 XT, the engine fundamentally refuses to run reliably.

Disappointing mid-Hunt Crashes
There is nothing more upsetting than spending 15 to 25 minutes fighting a brutal, high-rank monster, only for the game to abruptly crash to the desktop right as you are about to slay it. I have literally never had a single day of play where this game did not crash on me. You are constantly playing with anxiety, waiting for the next inevitable error.

Hoping for a Brighter Side (The DLC Dilemma)
If you love the franchise, I still recommend it. The underlying game is phenomenal and a joy to play when it actually works. It just desperately needs a stability patch. If you can tolerate daily crashes for the sake of amazing gameplay, pick it up. Otherwise, wait for the pre-DLC optimization patch.

It's a AAA Monhun game that looks godawful. Performance went from an utter disaster at launch to something approaching acceptable now, but it really isn't enough for how much time has passed. The gameplay isn't as bad as some might want you to think, but there's a lot of immersion and small gameplay things that got bulldozed for a more AAA experience, which really detracts from the special feel of Monhun games in the past. This is definitely a side-grade at best, and not really worth playing unless you're a diehard Monhun fan that has to play each one. I really hope the expansion makes things better, but at this point, I'm extremely doubtful.

For whats its worth. The game is somewhat decently optimized. Its playable and enjoyable without much stuttering so thats good.. Atleast on my pc specs. Unlike the beta and launch it was horrible. If the game is not on sale i do not recommend it. 

Playing through the game its been fun, i just hope more optimization patch comes in to help more and more hunters come in. With the DLC on the horizon i just hope my favourite Tigrex comes back and cause havoc to the world again XD

the optimization is horrid and I had to get mods just to be able to play it properly. Even now, with the lowest graphic settings, I still tend to get fatal errors. does this make the game itself bad? NO. the game is amazing but please be aware of possible issues with optimization

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the campaign and low-rank quests are too easy, lacking significant challenge until the endgame content.

citations.review_text:
TLDR - If youre a MH fan, there's nothing egregious about this game, get it if you have the specs and cash. Never played MH before, youre better off getting whatever MH game is going for cheapest at the moment and seeing if you like that.

This is my second monster hunter game after sunbreak. Got Rise on switch at launch and played through sunbreak on pc. Got this game a year after release with all the updates and performance patches, on top of it being 60% off. I would say that it's been worth it, both to wait and to buy this game in general.

General Impressions- I would say it's a great action game with a middling story that is better in concept than it is in execution. It has a great, unique roster that (mostly) feel good to fight. Environments are amazingly detailed and I love how the weather and effects add cinematography to the fights.

Combat - For the most part, much of the low and high rank story quests are really easy, you practically never need to prepare for a specific hunt in the story, but are made up for by the fantastic presentation and first impressions of the fights. Perfect guards, offsets, and power clashes make hunts feel action-packed without losing the more grounded nature of the game. 9/10-star monsters are where the real challenges lie after you have a set of fully upgraded armour + weapons, however some 7/8 star monsters will give you a run for your money, especially because some quests have a lower time limit. 

The new monsters feel great to fight, especially the apex of the desert and Ice cliffs. Attacks look threatening, well telegraphed and feel amazing to guard/dodge/counter. Monsters also have weak point windows after certain attacks that feel great to hit.

Non-hunting gameplay - This game being "open world" amounts to having a hub at every biome that you can leave and enter as you please with no load screens. Some biomes connect seamlessly through a singular path, but it really is only for story purposes, where you ride your mount…

You're better off playing MHWorld than MHWilds. Here's my opinion on the game.

The game is still unoptimized and still runs like ass that it feels so unsatisfying to play the game. Gathering materials for gear and hunting monsters are extremely easy - including the final bosses - that it doesn't even feel rewarding anymore. But the worst feature in the game, in my opinion, are the maps. They're kind of a little boring and dull - compared to World at least. Traversing through them feels really tedious. And you pair that with unoptimized gameplay - you get a really tedious experience. I, by no means, hate the franchise - I love monster hunter and I've been playing since I was a kid. But this game is kind of a little boring and tedious. Let's see if the expansion DLC changes that.

The most important part of the actual gameplay was fairly good. Didn't care much for the campaign story. Menus and UI are awful as always with Monster Hunter games, hoped for this to be vastly improved over MH:World but it's as terrible as ever. 

Praying for a lot of improvements in these areas for the 2027 DLC. A significant bump in difficulty would be nice too as the base game was too easy for the majority of it's run.

grounded enough like world, "fun" enough like rise, they remove the bs from both games but that probably turned some people off. performance finally reached a bearable state too, but still looks like ps 2. 

as for difficulty it's enough at endgame but at low rank it's too easy, rise wasn't like this even if i came to rise after mastering world so the base game felt too short.

i like the link party system since i can get auto invites or invites my friend when starting a quest so we dont have to manually check if the other person is already in the quest and wheteher we can join or not unlike world and rise, but it still fell short since you can't exactly join the assignment quest with your friends before the combat phase begins so you still need to wait.

+ Learning curve felt a lot better compared to World:Iceborn and Rise:Sunbreak
+ There was an actual story to develop the environment and monsters
+ The music was great (As always with all monhun music)
+ Most weapons got buffed so their skill floors are much lower now, allowing newcomers the chance to learn multiple weapons

・The cons:

+ Split weapons and armor skills/decos
+ Coming from both World:Iceborn and Rise:Sunbreak, the games felt too easy

+ Charm farming is just a copy paste from Sunbreak without the actual fun part (anomaly inve…

Decent

The performance is garbage and the game is way too easy

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game incorporates NPC support hunters into gameplay.

citations.review_text:
Played 142 hours minus 20-30 afk/sleeping etc. Did pretty much all, entirely solo. I really like the new added NPC supporters, amazing, keep them pls. I'm Rank 120. I never told anyone, but I actually hate killing the monsters, maybe they can add some “pacifist” option, that we automatically catch the monsters :P. I donate to WAP in real life etc. so...I know, it's just a game. Solo is way harder than party play as always. Do I have to write why? NPC's help a lot though. 

First of all, I love the open world idea they implemented in wilds, seeing animals running around and such, it feels alive. Graphics are amazing, some of the best in MH games, 4k here. I had no problems with bugs or so, I had one shut down/bug were game closed. 

I personally think people are very harsh with this MH game. I found it quite great, funny, entertaining. I found Nata annoying in start, but the boy have his heart in the right place(you should never kill as the first thing), and why does Nata and Rove get to sit so close to Alma's beep, unfair xD. That Erik is still quite strange though, lol, man or woman? Those wudwuds are totally copies of evoks from Star Wars? 

Let's take the “easier” people assert. I played world(iceborne with health sponges – in fact I still need to complete iceborne, I bought wilds on sale before I completed it), did Rise/Sunbreak entirely solo, and I can tell you, Wilds is not that much easier? Well, there are some elements, but I didn't know in start. You can fill your inventory at camps(a bit op), the seikret can come pick you up and such. Listen people, just don't use it? Use rarity 1 gear etc.? Are you idiots or something? Whining about something you can make harder yourselves. Also, CAPCOM could make the game single player based, add easy/medium/hard and hard hardcore mode, where you lose your character if you chart one time. Then they could also add challenge modes, where you could add take “cannot use potions”, “monsters deal 2 x damage and have 3 x speed”…

Monster Hunter Wilds feels like their best iteration so far. I'm really not sure why it has such mixed reviews. It's been an absolute blast playing through it. I've worked my way through the story and most of the end game content, including (at the time of writing this) the final Gogmazios fight. It feels really accessible compared to MH World, which makes it a lot more enjoyable for me. I really like the addition of Support Hunters and the Seikret. There's a lot more monster variety in this as well, which I like, instead of just all dragon-like monsters. The world is beautiful and immersive. And I like how it's ALMOST like an MMO with the addition of lobbies that allow you to spend time in the towns with other players and join their quests. Personally, I cannot wait for the DLC to come out.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that weapon modifications for bowguns were removed and replaced with selectable special ammo types.

citations.review_text:
[salty yappening for devs]

Man I used to main HBG in MHW(orld), I came back to have the MH wilds version explained to me and completely lost interest again... They took away the melee attack and they made some overcomplicated systems (which I dont mind they are usually good at this) that only constrict your gameplay even more. You cant choose your playstyle with any of the Wilds ranged weapons, you are locked in one. 

I hope they completely rework them in the dlc. They did some significant good advancements in wilds, I hope they make the weapons a fun vehicle for exploring it cause right now I was out as soon as I finished the story. Theres like 3-4 weapon types they made super well on their new mechanics that have a good flow and good skill expression. After youre tired of using them its better to close the game than to try any of the others... My goat is Lance, Switch blade, Longsword and Insect Glave in wilds. ( heard blowhorn is peak too )

Also they did nothing with the weather system they hyped in the pre release materials. I hope they do

And when I saw like 5 Yian Kut Kus or sand worms in the same fight I thought they made some kind of herd system that you get weaker monsters hunting in flocks which would make them survive more than the early game and also give a fresh take on the combat strats we each have (weak point system is pretty OP so the hunters could handle it). Thats not something they hyped thats some idea I thought would be fun... 

I think the devs wanted to make weak monsters get played more in late game (which I love) thats why in MHW they made you replay them three times (low rank, high rank, master rank) and then gave some of them tempered and arch tempered versions, and then you had the whole free roam area that was like a master rank ++ that you got to hunt them a fourth time... I get it, they are right for wanting to do this, weak monsters are some of the best fights in MH, a herd system where you would have to fight 5-6( 10? as many as…

A pretty solid entry to the series, with a pretty decent roster of Monsters (which could have been a little bit bigger, but the Title Updates expanded added a handful of Monsters in) and none of them feel particularly annoying to hunt. The weapons feel a lot more accessible, especially with the new Offset counters (these allow you to perform a follow-up at a certain threshold, but not every weapon has one) and the Perfect Guard (This lets you clash with the monster, and knock it back), although they're still diverse enough for you to find one you like and combat retains its fluidity from Rise, but still keeps it somewhat grounded like in World.

Focus mode is pretty good, but it can be abused on wounds to down a monster for a long period of time, trivialising a good number of them if you build around wounds & focus attacks.

Mods have been seemingly removed from Bowguns (instead letting you chose your special ammo type) and I hope this isn't permanent for the series (even though most mods have been applied to the default moveset I still wish reload/ deviation mods were still a thing.)

Weapons:

Long Sword: A counter-heavy weapon that relies on you to read monsters' attacks and time your sheathe or foresight counters to retain your flow, all while filling up the spirit gauge to power up certain moves.

Great Sword: A powerful weapon that is slow, but can deal massive damage with its charged attacks, It does also come with both a guard and an offset attack.

Sword and Shield: A fast weapon with minor guarding capabilities

Dual Blades: A fast hitting weapon that also allows you to run monsters through a blender (the focus attack has you spin down the length of the monster, much like its jumping attacks from some of the previous games)

Charge Blade: A bigger Sword and Shield that can transform into an axe, which can either be used as a SnS with a bigger focus on statuses/ elements and a heavy-hitting axe finisher, or it can be purely used in axe mode whenever you hav…
